mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when GDPC1 shows a sustained decline over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves on expectations of increased economic output.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek higher returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with low interest rates
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a weakening demand for housing, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing sector is a significant component of the economy.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when HOUST decreases by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 300,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 300,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 300,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS shows a sustained increase over two consecutive months.
